concepts.title: Oceans and Continents: The Blue Planet

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Oceans and Continents: The Blue Planet' refers to.
questions.a: Seen from space the Earth looks blue because almost three-fourths of its surface is water; the largest water bodies are oceans and the largest continuous land areas are continents.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Oceans and Continents: The Blue Planet'.
questions.a: The blue planet divides into great waters and great lands, and both shape climate, life and history.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Oceans and Continents: The Blue Planet', in plain ASCII form.

concepts.title: Water and Land in the Two Hemispheres

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Water and Land in the Two Hemispheres' refers to.
questions.a: Oceans and continents are not spread equally: maps drawn from above the North and South Poles show that most land gathers in the Northern Hemisphere while water dominates the Southern Hemisphere.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Water and Land in the Two Hemispheres'.
questions.a: Looking from each pole gives two different pictures of the same planet.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Water and Land in the Two Hemispheres' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Distribution of Water and Land (source: fees102.txt, Distribution of Water and Land)

concepts.title: The Seven Continents of the Earth

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'The Seven Continents of the Earth' refers to.
questions.a: The Earth's land is grouped into seven continents: Asia, the largest, then Africa, North America, South America, Antarctica, Europe and Australia; islands such as ours sit near or within them.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'The Seven Continents of the Earth'.
questions.a: Continents are the great land containers of the world, each with its own size, climate and life.

questions.q: Under which section is 'The Seven Continents of the Earth' taught, and from which source text?

concepts.title: The Five Oceans of the Earth

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'The Five Oceans of the Earth' refers to.
questions.a: The world's waters form five oceans, the Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Arctic and Southern, joined into one great body that stirs climate and carries ships between continents.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'The Five Oceans of the Earth'.
questions.a: All oceans are one connected water body, divided by human naming into five.

questions.q: Under which section is 'The Five Oceans of the Earth' taught, and from which source text?
